Control settings for joinpoint fitting

Source: R/joinpoint.R
jp_control.Rd

Settings of the grid search, model selection, confidence intervals, AAPC ranges and random number generation.

Usage

jp_control(
  min_obs_end = 2,
  min_obs_between = 2,
  n_grid = 0,
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_perm = 4499,
  n_exceed = NULL,
  perm_seed = 7160,
  n_resample = 5001,
  eq_seed = 10000,
  eq_final_only = TRUE,
  seed_mode = c("constant", "vary"),
  alpha_apc = 0.05,
  alpha_aapc = 0.05,
  alpha_joinpoint = 0.05,
  alpha_jump = 0.05,
  aapc_full = TRUE,
  aapc_last = NULL,
  aapc_ranges = NULL,
  madwd = NULL,
  dds_cutoffs = c(10, 200),
  infeasible = c("reduce", "recommended", "skip"),
  tau_interval = c("lerman", "literal"),
  time_budget = 60
)

Arguments

min_obs_end

Minimum number of observations from a joinpoint to either end of the data, excluding the joinpoint itself when it falls on an observation (1 to 9, default 2).

min_obs_between

Minimum number of observations between two joinpoints, excluding joinpoints that fall on observations (0 to 9, default 2).

n_grid

Number of grid points placed between adjacent observed x values in the grid search (0 to 9, default 0).

alpha

Overall significance level of the sequential permutation test.

n_perm

Number of randomly permuted data sets for the permutation test (default 4499).

n_exceed

Optional early stopping of the permutation and likelihood ratio tests (Besag and Clifford 1991): simulation stops once n_exceed simulated statistics reach the observed one, at simulation L, and the p value is n_exceed / L. NULL runs all n_perm simulations. Values of 10 to 20 save most of the time of tests that do not reject.

perm_seed

Random number seed for the permutation test (NULL for the current random number stream). The global random number state is saved before the seed is set and restored afterwards.

n_resample

Number of resampled data sets for the empirical quantile confidence intervals (default 5001).

eq_seed

Random number seed for the empirical quantile method (NULL for the current random number stream). The global random number state is saved before the seed is set and restored afterwards.

eq_final_only

Use the empirical quantile method only for the final selected model; other models get parametric intervals.

seed_mode

"constant" uses the same seed for every cohort; "vary" uses seed * g + (g - 1) (modulo 2^31 - 1) for cohort g.

alpha_apc, alpha_aapc, alpha_joinpoint, alpha_jump

Significance levels for the APC, AAPC, joinpoint location and jump or comparability ratio intervals.

aapc_full

Compute the AAPC over the full range of the data.

aapc_last

Integer vector (up to two values) of "Last X observations" AAPC ranges.

aapc_ranges

List of up to seven numeric c(start, end) ranges anywhere within the data range.

madwd

Minimum APC difference worth detecting, in percentage points (NULL to disable).

dds_cutoffs

Cutoffs c < d of the data dependent selection.

infeasible

What to do when a cohort has too few observations for the requested kmax under the placement constraints: "reduce" lowers kmax to the largest feasible value, "recommended" uses the recommended maximum for the cohort, and "skip" leaves the cohort out. A warning is given in every case.

tau_interval

Parametric interval of joinpoint locations: "lerman" (Lerman 1980) or the more conservative "literal" variant Q (1 + k / (n - p)) F, which reproduces some published intervals.

time_budget

Approximate computing time, in seconds, allowed for the exhaustive search when kmax is left to its recommended value. The recommended maximum is lowered, with a message, when the search (with its permutation tests or resamples) would take longer; the budget is an estimate, not a deadline, and Inf removes it. An explicit kmax is always honored.

Value

A list of class jp_control.

References

Besag J, Clifford P (1991). Sequential Monte Carlo p-values. Biometrika 78:301-304.

Examples

jp_control(n_grid = 1, aapc_last = c(5, 10))
